gmm.support: very strong support for two groups
gmm.verdict: ΔBIC = +22.8 (one group 12539.7, two groups 12516.9): very strong support for two groups. BIC compares Gaussian shapes, and a single skewed cloud can earn two components, so this is evidence, not proof. But its two groups are barely the DS / IED split (adjusted Rand 0.00, where 1 is the same split and 0 is chance; 64% of events the same): two Gaussians fit the cloud's SHAPE better than one, which a single skewed spectrum also does. Read the split-axis histogram before reading this as two populations.

measure.filter_label: DS filter, 5–100 Hz, 60 Hz mains out

rule: Pooled over 9 recordings from 9 mice, in pooled raw units: k = 1: one cluster, so no split -- every event is called DS (1475 DS, 0 IED, 2 not measured; 6 resolved only with a half-width search widened past 50 ms).

scale.why: Pooled raw units, z-scored once across the pool: differences in size between mice stay visible, impedance and placement included.

split_axis.unit: z, 0 at the midpoint, DS negative
